reason: Revision of the five questions judged 'revise' in the first review (op-threshold-block, op-tie-block-transport, op-layer-period, op-continuum-ties-blocks, op-deformation-boundary). Topics are unchanged. Each statement now carries the status and range that the published records actually give (proved / certified / informal / observed / heuristic / open), the premises that the review found contradicted by the records are restricted to the regimes or parameters where the records show them, the two length scales k^(2/3) and k^(1/3) are kept apart, and every question ends with an explicit sufficiency criterion and a one-sentence boundary against the neighbouring questions (including the two admitted ones, op-central-window and op-left-right-asymmetry). Record coordinates are those of the instance at frontier revision 184; the right half is informally proved and the left interior is what remains of the root.

questions.statement: In four regimes the records show the one-step difference d = b_{n,k} - b_{n,k-1} decided at a relative margin of order k^(-1/3): the centre t = (n-2k)/k^(2/3) -> 0, where the two compared terms share their leading constant and differ by (2/I_0) k^(-1/3) (I_0 = Gamma(2/3)/3^(1/3)); the first layer at fixed lambda = k/n in (1/2,1), where the margin is (m(lambda)+o(1)) k^(-1/3) (informal proof); the second layer lambda in (1/3,1/2), where the predicted margin is m_3(lambda) k^(-1/3) with min m_3 ~ 15.34 (conjecture with measurements); and the right critical window at finite c, where the margin falls short of its universal limit by D(x-hat) c^(-1/3), D ~ 5-9.5 (observation). In the first layer (informal proof) and conjecturally in the second, the mechanism is a rare cluster of k^(1/3) heavy sites carried by one component that lands within O(k^(2/3)) above the capacity k, set against a smooth background curvature that stays O(1): the convex-kink identity d = Conv - Kink shows that the moment test measures two pieces of amplitude D I_0 k^(1/3) whose difference is the finite layer curvature. Two other regimes look different in the records and are not assumed to share this premise: inside the central window at fixed t in [t_0,T] the moment ratio converges to a k-independent profile R_inf(t) (maximum ~2.25 at t ~ 4) and the margin is O(1), and in the pole regime n >> k^(3/2) the mean E[Z] ~ kappa_k n grows linearly so that E^2 dominates the other moment terms, while the concentrated blocks are prime blocks of size just BELOW k, in a boundary layer of width k/sigma_k; no k^(1/3) heavy-site mass and no k^(-1/3) margin is shown there. The question: what is the local limit law of the threshold-adjacent component in the k^(-1/3) regimes - the law of its size offset above k (scale k^(2/3)), of its heavy-site count (scale k^(1/3)), of its tie/blocked status, and of its first finite-size correction - and is it one and the same object at the centre, in the first layer, in the second layer and in the right window, with only the macroscopic intensity (B_lambda + D_lambda in the first layer, the boundary flux D_3 in the second) changing? Two scales inside the cluster must be kept apart: the cluster sits at stopping depth O(k^(2/3)) above k (92-95% of the blocked-maximum loss comes from chains that descended to within 0.5 k^(2/3) of k), while the gain/loss boundary in chain-endpoint distance is a band of the narrower scale k^(1/3) (heuristically r* ~ 0.63 k^(1/3)); a local law must resolve both. A sufficient answer gives one local law from which the regime constants 2/I_0 (centre), m(lambda) and m_3(lambda) (layers) and D(x-hat) (right window) are recovered, and states whether the window-interior object (two components, O(1) margin) and the pole-regime boundary-layer block are the same local object seen under different intensities or genuinely different objects; or it shows that the k^(-1/3) regimes themselves involve different local objects. Boundary: op-central-window asks for the t-profiles and the landmark coincidence of the window; op-layer-period asks for the macroscopic constants kappa_r, D_r, m_r and their hand-over to the pole regime; op-continuum-ties-blocks asks for the continuum identification of ties and blocks in the right window; this question asks only whether the threshold-local object is shared.

Two scales: ra52a3c0... section 5 - 92-95% of kE[H_k] comes from chains that descended to within k + 0.5 k^(2/3) (stopping depth; producer's heuristic picture; D* = 0.542 k^(2/3)); r20df549... section 3.5 Lemma 3.2 (proved: hazard h_pi(r) -> beta_r/(e - sum_{j<r} beta_j), 1/e at r = 0) and section 3.6b (r* ~ 0.63 k^(1/3) is a heuristic prediction of the depth-law model; observed r* = 1, 4, 8, 13). The k^(2/3) stopping depth and the k^(1/3) endpoint band are different scales. The index module large-subtree-path-and-borel-renewal insists that the global chains (maximum-tree chain, nested block path, late-maximum chain, prime renewal) are different processes; this question presupposes that distinction and asks about local structure only. Conjectural.

questions.statement: The one-step difference is a difference of two positive counts, b_{n,k} - b_{n,k-1} = 2E_{n,k} - B_{n,k-1} (even ties at the maximum minus blocked maxima), of the same order and with relative gap of order n^(-1/3) in the right bulk. On the right half (k+1 <= n <= 2k-1) an exact decomposition by chain endpoint is proved, and the sign of each endpoint class is the comparison of two quantities: a hazard - the probability that the forest under an endpoint at distance r above k contains a tree of size exactly k - which converges (proved) to h_pi(r) with h_pi(0) = 1/e and h_pi(r) ~ 1/(2r), against the class's tie gain g ~ E[N(N-1)]/k. From this, large-n computations (binary64, lambda in {0.6, 0.7, 0.8}, n <= 3*10^4) show a three-stage sign -,+,- by endpoint: chains ending within r*(k) of the threshold lose, chains ending somewhat further gain, shallow chains lose; r* = 1, 4, 8, 13 at n = 600, 3000, 10^4, 3*10^4 (lambda = 0.7), the deep-class loss is certified exactly at (n,k) = (300,210), (600,420), (1000,700), and a depth-law model built on the published Palm law predicts r* ~ 0.63 k^(1/3) heuristically (the needed upper bound on the endpoint-conditioned pair count is unproved). At small n (<= 110) most increasing positions are instead +- (1277 of 1610), so the three-stage shape is a large-n phenomenon. Slicing by H_k, the h = 0 slice is always >= 0 while h >= 1 slices turn negative well before the mode, and the site-wise comparison already fails at site k: the positivity is a global compensation that no H-preserving slice-wise or site-wise injection can exhibit. Where does the compensation live? (i) Is there a pairing or transport that carries blocked-maximum mass to tie mass between endpoint classes - in the narrowest sense one that changes only the last step of the same chain (endpoint displacement O(1) or o(k^(1/3))), in a wider sense one whose endpoint displacement is O(k^(1/3)), the width of the loss band - or must any transport that accounts for the sign move mass across endpoint distances >> k^(1/3) or between different global structures (non-local)? (ii) How close to a bijection must it be - the relative gap is n^(-1/3), so asymptotically almost bijective - and does that exclude every argument that loses a constant factor locally? (iii) What replaces the chain-endpoint classes on the left half (n > 2k), where the vertices of size > k form a tree with side branches and H_k can exceed 1: is there a leaf-wise decomposition with the same two-ingredient sign test? A sufficient answer exhibits an explicit transport in one of the senses of (i) that accounts for the sign geography on the right (the three-stage shape and the growth of r*), or proves that no transport with endpoint displacement O(k^(1/3)) exists; and gives, or rules out, the leaf-wise analogue on the left. Boundary: op-left-right-asymmetry asks which structural feature separates the two halves and whether the right-side unconditioning device has a left analogue; this question asks for the combinatorial pairing behind the sign and its left-half form.

questions.statement: In the right critical window x = (n-k)/n^(2/3) the two positive counts in b_{n,k} - b_{n,k-1} = 2E_{n,k} - B_{n,k-1} have conjectured universal limits: Theorem C (informal outline, not written out) gives c^(4/3) B_{n,c-1}/p_n -> B-hat(x-hat)/(2 pi) and c^(4/3) e_n/p_n -> E-hat(x-hat)/pi for the two-tie count e_n, and numerically (2 E-hat - B-hat)/(2 pi) = -f' where f is the published limit density of the normalised deficit: the slope of the critical density is 'two-car tie density minus blocked-maximum density', and the mode x_* = 0.5996 is where the two densities balance (the zero of the limit margin is x-hat_0 = 0.59963, equal to x_* to four digits). Two things are already known about this identity. From the published third-order local limits, c^(4/3) (V - B)/p_n -> -f' holds for V = 2E (all even ties), so, given Theorem C, the identity is equivalent to the statement that four or more cars tying at the maximum are negligible on the window scale. And a heuristic identification - threshold sites (capacity exactly k) <-> the increments dR of the Brownian running maximum R, with q_j dx = E[R^j e^(-Lambda) dR]/j! - reproduces the mode-constant limits lim eps_c = -0.29710, lim E[Z_c H_c] = 0.44299, lim F_c = 0.14589, with which the measured values (n = 200 ... 20000) are compatible, moving toward them for n >= 1000 though not monotonically. What is asked beyond this reduction: which events of (R, Lambda) are 'two cars tie at the maximum' and 'the maximum is blocked by capacity', so that E-hat and B-hat are identified as functionals of (R, Lambda) and Theorem C, the identity and the mode-constant limits follow from the continuum law rather than from numerics? A sufficient answer (a) proves Theorem C or otherwise identifies E-hat and B-hat as functionals of (R, Lambda); (b) proves the threshold-site <-> dR identification and the interchange of window limits with differences that the mode-constant computation uses; (c) reconciles E-hat, B-hat with the existing continuum functions of the boundary comparisons, H_S = -2[h_2 f'' + 3 h_3 f'] and H_C = 2 h_2 h_2' - 3 h_3 f' (H_S = 2 H_C - 2 h_2 q_0'); and (d) says what the same event identification gives in the central window where two components contribute (S = X^(1) + X^(2)). Boundary: op-central-window asks for the t-profiles and the landmark coincidence of the central window; op-threshold-block asks whether the threshold-local object is shared across regimes; this question asks only for the continuum identification of the two counts.
